title.narrative: Revolutionising the agri-solar space by developing an efficient and affordable IoT enabled mill

description.narrative:
This project enabled Agsol to create the most efficient, smart and affordable small grain mill ever developed – the MicroMill. At project close we have finished field trials of the v1 MicroMill and are well progressed to deliver on the next v2 iteration, which has the potential to scale across multiple markets and to out-compete diesel mills in many off-grid contexts.
The MicroMill developed under this project is an entirely new innovation that is 2-3 times more efficient than other small electric mills. The starting point for the project was to identify a suitable direct drive brushless DC (BLDC) motor. The rationale for a direct drive motor is that it is the most efficient and cost effective approach to transfer electrons to shaft power, as there are no transfer losses or additional components.
More than 15 BLDC motors were extensively tested for their potential to power a high-speed direct drive milling machine. Motors were put through their paces using a variety of endurance and destructive testing procedures at our R&D facility in China. We built a custom test bed that monitored and logged all vital motor diagnostics during these tests. Based upon the results, a 400W high speed BLDC motor was selected to take forward.
In testing the motors with a configurable milling chamber across different speed and power settings, we learned that much conventional and published information about milling efficiencies did not apply at low power micro-milling scale.
We also learned how critical it is for efficiency to keep the motor precisely loaded; if too much or too little material enters the chamber the efficiency tapers off dramatically.
Small milling machines on the market require the operator to manually manage the flow of material entering the chamber, which requires a level of technical knowledge to balance the flow rate with the load on the machine. This becomes increasingly difficult at low power milling.
To overcome this challenge our next technological development was to design and build an automatic feed control mechanism. The auto-feeder electro-mechanically connects the flow rate of material to the load on the motor to maintain an ideal load for maximum efficiency. Our auto-feeder is an industry first for small scale mills.
The other major benefit of the auto-feeder is it means any non-technical person can operate the machine and therefore it has a much larger potential customer base. As long as the grain is clean, the operator needs no technical knowledge and machine takes care of everything else.
Because the auto-feeder needs to respond to what the motor is experiencing, we also needed to develop a custom PCB that could communicate between the two components. The PCB was also responsible for managing the BLDC motor driver and a number of other onboard power control and safety features.
